claim: `@server` / `@client*` are privileged built-ins: a micro/logic/hyper processor reads the null constant from them, so the instruction runs but the branch never takes. Only a world processor (privileged) sees a real value.
why: GlobalVars registers these names with putEntry(name, value, true) (:81-90), and get(name, privileged) returns vars.get("null") when !privileged && privilegedNames.contains(name) (:253-256). Nothing throws, which is why a program ported from a world processor to a normal one silently loses the branch.
heuristic_note: A world processor reads these for real, but a .mlog file does not name its block, so analyse() cannot tell it apart and still prints the INFO. That is why this is INFO and not WARN; treat it as a reminder, not a verdict.
